plates.quality_reason: Flow-first: a teach diagram, chart, counter or timeline is a £0 code graphic. No Flow mint.
plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, the 5-date timeline completes: 1849 (John Snow publishes On the Mode of Communication of Cholera proposing waterborne transmission) · 31 Aug – 8 Sep 1854 (616 die around the Soho Broad Street pump; Snow maps the outbreak and convinces the parish to remove the pump handle on 8 Sep) · 1854–1855 (Snow's South London Grand Experiment proves 315 vs 37 deaths per 10,000 houses; Henry Whitehead traces the Broad Street index case to a leaking cesspool 2 ft 8 in from the well; Filippo Pacini describes Vibrio cholerae) · 1859–1866 (Bazalgette builds 82 miles of London intercepting sewers; William Farr uses Snow's water-pipe method to pinpoint the 1866 East London outbreak) · 1883–1884 (Robert Koch isolates and cultures the cholera comma bacillus in Egypt and India).

teach_overlay.label: 1849–1884 TIMELINE · BAZALGETTE'S 82 MILES OF SEWERS · TREATED CHOLERA DEATHS: >50% → <1%
teach_overlay.detail: Animated 5-date timeline (1849 → 1883–1884) alongside Joseph Bazalgette's 82 miles of intercepting brick sewers and the drop in treated cholera fatality from >50% to <1%
teach_overlay.scale: replacing polluted river water with clean pipes and sewers — plus simple salt-and-sugar rehydration — cut the death rate of treated cholera from more than half of all patients to less than one in a hundred
